question: The trial for Meerut conspiracy took place under whose Viceroyalty?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Lord Irwin__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** **Meerut Conspiracy:**

__
 
• **​​The Meerut Conspiracy Case** was a controversial court case in British India in **1929** during the viceroyalty of **Lord Irwin**.
 
• It involved the **arrest and trial of 31 trade unionists and communists** for allegedly conspiring to overthrow the British government.
 
• The accused were members of the **Communist Party of India** and the** All-India Trade Union Congress**.
 
• The case was a **significant event** in the history of the **Indian independence movement**, as it highlighted the growing influence of communist ideology in the **struggle against British rule**.
 
• The defendants were ultimately **convicted and sentenced to various terms of imprisonment**.
 
• The case drew **widespread attention and criticism** from both **Indian** and **international observers**.
 
• The trial was seen as a symbol of **British repression **and** intolerance** towards political dissent in India.
 
• The case also led to increased solidarity between the** Indian nationalist movement and the international communist movement**.
 
• The Meerut Conspiracy Case served as a **catalyst** for the growth of communist influence in India in the following decades.
 
• It remains a significant episode in the history of the Indian left and its role in the struggle for independence.

• **Lord Chelmsford:**

 
 
• Lord Chelmsford, also known as Frederic John Napier Thesiger, served as the Viceroy of India from 1916 to 1921.
 
• He was appointed by King George V during a crucial period in British rule in India, which included World War I and the aftermath of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
 
• Lord Chelmsford's tenure was marked by significant political and social unrest, including widespread protests and strikes by Indian nationalists.
 
• After leaving India, he continued to be involved in public service and held various government positions in the United Kingdom.
 
• Lord Chelmsford passed away in 1933 at the age of 69.
 
• His legacy continues to be debated and analyzed in historical studies of British colonial rule in India.
 
 
 
• **Lord Reading:**
 
 
• Lord Reading, also known as Rufus Daniel Isaacs, served as the Viceroy of India from 1921 to 1925.
 
• He was appointed by King George V during a critical period in British rule in India, which included significant political and social upheaval.
 
• Lord Reading's tenure was marked by efforts to address growing demands for Indian self-government and independence.
 
• He was ultimately succeeded by Lord Irwin as Viceroy of India.
 
• After leaving India, he continued to be involved in public service and held various government positions in the United Kingdom.
 
• Lord Reading passed away in 1935 at the age of 75.
 
• His tenure as Viceroy continues to be studied and debated in historical analyses of British colonial rule in India.
 
 
 
• **Lord Irwin:**
 
 
• Lord Irwin, also known as Edward Frederick Lindley Wood, served as the Viceroy of India from 1926 to 1931.
 
• He was appointed by King George V to oversee British rule in India during a critical period of the Indian independence movement.
 
• Lord Irwin is best known for his efforts to initiate dialogue with Indian nationalist leaders, including Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• Lord Irwin's tenure as Viceroy marked a pivotal moment in British-Indian relations and the ongoing struggle for Indian independence.
 
• After leaving India, he continued to be involved in public service and held various government positions in the United Kingdom.
 
• Lord Irwin passed away in 1984 at the age of 90.
 
 
 
• **Lord Harding:**
 
 
• Lord Harding, also known as Charles Harding, served as the Viceroy of India from 1910 to 1916.
 
• He was appointed by King George V during a critical period in British rule in India, which included World War I and growing demands for Indian self-government.
 
• Lord Harding's tenure was marked by efforts to address various social and political issues in India, including labor unrest and demands for constitutional reform.
 
• He was ultimately succeeded by Lord Chelmsford as Viceroy of India.
 
• After leaving India, he continued to be involved in public service and held various government positions in the United Kingdom.
 
• Lord Harding passed away in 1928 at the age of 65.
 
• His tenure as Viceroy continues to be studied and debated in historical analyses of British colonial rule in India.
